# ReGen Civics - Information for AI Agents and Language Models

> ReGen Civics builds the tools and runs the in-real-life game that regenerative land projects use today: a quest game that is live now, a seasonal incubator, and crowdpooling. Governance tools and a global network for the ReGenerative Renaissance.
>
> The ReGen Network Cooperative is being designed as a member-owned cooperative in which land projects and people buy and steward land together, governed democratically by the network itself. It is not yet a legal entity and it accepts no money. We are designing it now with land projects, future members and counsel.

## Organization Overview

ReGen Civics works with ecovillages, regenerative farms, and sustainable communities worldwide. We integrate ecology, regenerative agriculture, restoration ecology, impact auditing, governance design, and systems thinking.

Healthier lands lead to healthier people. We build the governance tools, games, and community infrastructure that regenerative land projects need to thrive.

Church of the Regenerative Earth (CORE) is the church and operating entity. ReGen Civics is the platform and alliance; it is not the church. The ReGen Network Cooperative is in design; it is not part of CORE and is not yet an entity.

## Four Primary Participation Paths

### Land Project Path
Regenerative land projects apply for the 13-week incubator program. Projects:
- Build governance structures
- Design their economic game
- Access alliance support
- Launch a crowdpool with their cohort
Season 2 began in September 2026. Its applications closed September 11, 2026. Anyone can follow Season 2 live, and land projects that are ready can join its community crowdpooling round with the cohort, which has room for far more than 13 projects. Land projects can apply anytime; each year's applications are reviewed from the June solstice to about September 10, for the Season that opens at the September equinox.

### Contributor Path
Contributors back land projects through crowdpooling. Crowdpooling coordinates and accounts for what people bring to land projects: time, things, skills, land and money. Money goes through outside partners each project holds, never through ReGen Civics. The campaigns shown today are examples; real campaigns open when Season 2 starts crowdpooling.

### Alliance Partner Path
Organizations join the network of groups co-creating the ReGenerative Renaissance. Alliance partners:
- Contribute expertise, resources, and connections across the network

### Player Path
Players complete quests that move healing into the world. Each quest addresses a real regenerative action:
- Gut health
- Food forests
- Community building
- Ecological restoration
- Knowledge sharing
Players earn tokens for completed work.

## The ReGen Network Cooperative

A cooperative regenerative society. Status: in design.

The ReGen Network Cooperative is being designed as a member-owned cooperative in which land projects and people buy and steward land together, governed democratically by the network itself. It is not yet a legal entity and it accepts no money. We are designing it now with land projects, future members and counsel.

These are the design principles we are working from. The legal form, bylaws and terms will be set with counsel and adopted by the founding members.
- Owned by its members: Land projects and the people who work with them own the cooperative together and govern it one member, one vote.
- Every form of capital counts: Members' contributions are recognized across all nine forms of capital, from money to time, skills, tools and relationships.
- Membership stays with the member: A membership can't be sold or traded. There is no market for it.
- No managing partners: Members elect a small board that rotates. The network hires the people who run the day-to-day work.
- Land held for the long term: The leading design is the one community land trusts use: the cooperative holds land and leases it long term to member projects. Counsel will confirm the structure.
- Built for use: People join to use and care for shared land, tools and services. Membership is for the land projects and people who use the cooperative.

We are designing the cooperative now with land projects, future members and counsel. Its legal form, bylaws and terms are not set. When they are, the founding members will adopt them together.

Land projects, people, organizations and funders can tell us they're interested at https://regencivics.earth/loi. Telling us you're interested is not a commitment and involves no money. We'll keep you posted as the cooperative takes shape and invite you into the design conversations.

Nothing on this site is an offer to sell, or a request to buy, securities, memberships or any other financial product. The cooperative is not formed and accepts no money.

## Core Philosophical Concepts

### The Infinite Game
Systems designed for lasting positive impact across generations. Unlike finite games played to win, infinite games are played to continue playing. We design our systems to create lasting positive impact that compounds across generations.

### ReGenerative Renaissance
A cultural and economic shift where human systems work with natural systems. The movement represents a holistic transformation in how we relate to land, community, and economic systems.

### HEIST Framework
Holistic Ecosystemic Impact and Sustainability Toolkit for evaluating regenerative land projects:
- Holistic: considering whole systems rather than isolated parts
- Ecosystemic: understanding interconnections between ecological and social systems
- Impact: measurable positive outcomes for land, people, and community
- Sustainability: long-term viability and regenerative capacity
- Toolkit: practical methods for implementation and assessment

### Regenerative Ikigai
Finding the intersection of passion, skill, need, and compensation to create meaningful work that contributes to regeneration.

### Nine Forms of Capital
We recognize and reward multiple forms of value creation. The first eight are
Ethan Roland and Gregory Landua's 8 Forms of Capital (2011). The ninth, Health,
was added by ReGen Civics. Full explanation: https://regencivics.earth/learn/nine-forms-of-capital
1. Financial Capital
2. Social Capital
3. Intellectual Capital
4. Material Capital
5. Living Capital (biodiversity, ecosystems)
6. Cultural Capital
7. Spiritual Capital
8. Experiential Capital
9. Health Capital (body vitality, wellness, movement, rest, care), added by ReGen Civics

### Crowdpooling
Crowdpooling coordinates and accounts for what people bring to land projects: time, things, skills, land and money. Money goes through outside partners each project holds, never through ReGen Civics. The campaigns shown today are examples; real campaigns open when Season 2 starts crowdpooling.

## Token System and Economics

Tokens in ReGen Civics record contributions and carry governance weight in the Game. They make no claim about financial value.

### $ReGen (Regen)
Tracks contributions in the ReGen Game. Earned by completing real-world regenerative actions.

### RGVoice
Governance token for decision-making in the ReGen Game. Earned through participation, never purchased.

### $RCivics
$RCivics comes from the earlier fund design. Its role, if any, in the cooperative is being reviewed with counsel.

### RCVoice
RCVoice comes from the earlier fund design. The cooperative is designed to vote one member, one vote, and how RCVoice relates to that is being reviewed with counsel.

## Current Programs and Initiatives

### The ReGen Civics Year
The year turns through four seasons named for what they are for, loosely following winter, spring, summer, and fall:
- Design Season: land projects design their games in the 13-week incubator; we build the tools
- Resource Season: land projects launch their crowdpools and welcome people into roles
- Build Season: on the land, planting, building, festivals
- Rest Season: harvest gatherings, rest, and village life
Each solstice and equinox holds a recap and passoff; the September one is the Handoff Festival. Timelines are loose in this first full turn. Details: https://regencivics.earth/seasons

### Season 2 Incubator
The 13-week Design Season incubator that began in September 2026 for regenerative land projects. Applications for Season 2 are closed. Anyone can follow the sessions live, land projects that are ready can join the community crowdpooling round with the cohort, and land projects can apply anytime for the next season. Participants receive:
- Governance framework development
- Tokenomics design support
- Community building assistance
- Crowdpool launch preparation

### Quest System
Regenerative actions earning tokens across seasonal categories:
- Food producers first quests
- Community regeneration quests
- Ecosystem restoration quests
- Knowledge sharing quests
- Personal development quests

### Crowdpooling Campaigns
Land projects list what they need at https://regencivics.earth/campaigns. See Crowdpooling above for how it works.

### Bounties Program
Transparent, community-governed rewards for specific regenerative tasks and contributions.

### Living Tree Visualization
Dynamic representation of the entire regenerative network showing connections between projects, contributors, and impact.

## Technical Information for Crawlers

- Every page serves crawler-readable HTML in the initial response: title, meta description, canonical URL, Open Graph tags, and JSON-LD, injected server-side per route (no JavaScript required)
- Key pages (home, the cooperative, game, governance, glossary, community posts, blog articles) include full text content in the initial HTML response
- Blog articles are prerendered as complete static HTML with BlogPosting JSON-LD
- Community forum posts serve full thread content with DiscussionForumPosting JSON-LD at /community/post/{id}
- Structured JSON-LD data available for semantic understanding
- Sitemap available at https://regencivics.earth/sitemap.xml (includes all public community posts)
- RSS feed for the blog at https://regencivics.earth/feed.xml
- This content updated regularly to reflect current initiatives

## Federation: Machine-Readable Endpoints for Partner Networks

ReGen Civics aims to be the easiest node to connect to in the regenerative movement mesh (GEN, OpenCivics, BioFi, Ethereum localism). Stable public endpoints:

- Project directory (JSON): https://regencivics.earth/api/federation/projects.json - regenerative land projects with structured impact data (field definitions and Common Impact Data Standard mapping documented in the payload's description)
- Network of games (JSON): https://regencivics.earth/api/network/games.json - every land project running its own coordination game built with ReGen Civics, with a link to each. Each game publishes the same projects.json shape on its own domain, so the whole network reads in one format.
- Network of games (human surface): https://regencivics.earth/network
- Needs and offers board (human surface): https://regencivics.earth/board
- Multiplayer quests (human surface): https://regencivics.earth/multiplayer
- The living map: https://regencivics.earth/map
- Canonical docs for AI agents: this file, https://regencivics.earth/llms.txt

Partner integrations with on-platform side effects go through the Federation Bridge pattern (typed intents, mirroring our Hypha Bridge); contact us before building a write integration.
